lines.text: Half the people in this study didn't notice they were talking to a different person.
lines.headline: A *different* person?

lines.text: In 1998, Daniel Simons and Daniel Levin had a stranger with a map stop people on campus to ask for directions.
lines.headline: Simons & Levin, *1998*

lines.text: Mid-chat, two workers carried a door right between them.
lines.headline: Watch the *door*

lines.text: Behind it, the stranger swapped places with someone else.
Of fifteen people, eight kept giving directions to a brand-new person.
lines.headline: ==8 of 15== missed it

lines.text: But that's not stupidity. Your brain doesn't save the whole scene, just the gist: a guy, a map, a question.
lines.headline: Your brain saves *the gist*

lines.text: So when details matter, a name, a number, a face, check them twice. And follow to test your eyes again.
lines.headline: Would *you* notice?

post.title: Half of People Didn't Notice They Were Talking to Someone New #shorts
post.description: Simons & Levin (1998): a stranger asked pedestrians for directions; two workers carried a door between them and a different person took his place. Only 7 of 15 noticed the swap. The brain keeps the gist, not the details: change blindness. #psychology #shorts #changeblindness #attention
